Two different questions — let me address both.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The server draft I just wrote is in place at `api/src/routes/recap.ts` + `api/src/lib/recap-aggregator.ts` + the `app.ts` wiring. It's a one-endpoint consumer for the CLI, so when it lands the CLI's fetch stack collapses to a single call.
- The local-storage idea solves a different problem: resilience when the server is slow / pending / down. Tool-time (shell/search/file-ops) and skills can be extracted from the transcript deterministically without the server. Labels genuinely require LLM classification, so those stay server-dependent.
- We don't have to pick one — server as primary, local as fallback is the right shape. We had a walker before and reverted it; bringing back a *narrower* version (just tool-time + skills, write into `metadata.json`, no classification) would be a small chunk of what we had.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## On the server draft

Drafted files (in entire.io working tree, ready for your review):

- `api/src/lib/recap-aggregator.ts` — `aggregateByAgent(rows, tokensByAgent?)` that rolls up labels/skills/MCP/toolMix per agent. Shared helper for me + contributors columns.
- `api/src/routes/recap.ts` — `GET /api/v1/me/recap?timeframe=&repo=&limit=` bearer-auth. Returns `{agents: {<name>: {me: AgentAggregate, contributors: AgentAggregate|null}}, contributors: {distinctUsers, totalTokens, totalCheckpoints}|null, ...}`.
- `api/src/app.ts` — mounts `v1.route("/me/recap", recapRoutes)` before the runner wildcard.

## On storing per-checkpoint data locally

Feasible to extract from the transcript during condense + write into `metadata.json`:

**Tool-time by category** — walk `tool_use` blocks in the transcript, bucket by name (`Bash` → shell, `Read/Write/Edit` → fileOps, `Grep/Glob` → search, `mcp__*` → mcp, `Agent/Skill` → agent, else → other), count + duration.

**Skills used** — parse `Skill` tool-use blocks in the transcript (Claude-specific; Codex/Gemini have equivalents). Each `Skill` call's `input.skill` field gives the skill name.

**NOT feasible locally** — labels (`bug_fix`, `feature_build`, etc.) are LLM-classified from the transcript by the server pipeline. No deterministic parse. Stays server-dependent.

### Proposed storage shape

Extend `CommittedMetadata` (the per-session metadata.json) with:

```go
type CommittedMetadata struct {
    ...
    // New:
    ToolTime   *ToolTimeProfile  `json:"tool_time,omitempty"`   // shell/fileOps/search/mcp/agent/other counts + durationMs
    SkillsUsed []string          `json:"skills_used,omitempty"` // deduped list per session
}
```

Then `projectCheckpoint` reads these fields from `CheckpointInfo`, surfaces them on `RecapCheckpoint.ToolProfile`/`SkillsUsed` without needing the server. The recap renderer would prefer local data when present; fall back to server enrichment when not.

## Scope question

Three paths:

**A.** Land the server draft first (test it end-to-end) → then add local fallback in a follow-up if you still want it.

**B.** Pause the server draft, build local storage first (re-derive tool-time + skills into metadata.json at condense time).

**C.** Do both in parallel.

My lean: **A**. The server endpoint is the common case (you're logged in, repo tracked). Local fallback is nice-to-have for edge cases. Land the fast path first, see how much the fallback adds.

Different fields come from different parts of the pipeline — so "no summaries" doesn't mean "no data."

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` is assembled at `api/src/lib/analysis-queue.ts:648` from TWO sources: `generateCheckpointAnalysis` (the **LLM** call, produces `extraction.labels` and `extraction.summary`) and `extractToolMetrics` (**deterministic** transcript parsing, produces `skillsUsed`, `mcpServersUsed`, `toolProfile`). Plus `extractModelsUsedFromSessionMetadata` for `modelsUsed`.
- If the LLM run is skipped or failed, `extraction` is absent (no labels, no summary) — but `skillsUsed`/`mcpServersUsed`/`toolProfile`/`modelsUsed` are STILL populated because they come from deterministic parsing that doesn't touch the LLM.
- If the whole pipeline never ran (no `analysis_json` written), nothing exists and the endpoint returns `status: "not_available"` or `"pending"`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## What survives without summaries

| Field | Source | Survives "no summaries"? |
|---|---|---|
| `extraction.labels` | LLM (generateCheckpointAnalysis) | ❌ — tied to summary generation |
| `extraction.summary` | LLM | ❌ — the thing that's missing |
| `skillsUsed` | deterministic parse of transcript | ✅ |
| `mcpServersUsed` | deterministic parse | ✅ |
| `toolProfile` | deterministic parse | ✅ |
| `modelsUsed` | session metadata | ✅ |
| `agentsUsed` | session metadata | ✅ |
| `total_transcript_tokens` | metadata sum | ✅ |
| `totalFilesChanged` | commit stats | ✅ |

## What this means for `entire recap`

- **If LLM is on, everything works** — both columns get labels, skills, mcp, tool-mix.
- **If LLM is off / rate-limited**, labels go empty on both me + contributor sides. Skills / MCP / tool-mix / tokens / counts all still populate. So the "Top skills", "MCP servers", "Tool mix" rows will have values; "Top labels" will show `—`.
- **If analysis never ran**, nothing — status is `pending` / `not_available`, everything shows `—`.

The local-fallback idea maps onto this cleanly: tool-time + skills are deterministic, so CLI can derive them from transcripts without the server. Labels always need the server because they require LLM classification.

**Recap-specific implication:** don't treat "no labels" as "no data." Render the deterministic fields (tokens, skills, mcp, tool-mix, counts) even when labels are empty, and show a specific hint for the labels row rather than collapsing the whole card.

1. Finalize the server `/me/recap` draft to also return the deterministic fields when `extraction` is missing (it already does since I read `skillsUsed`/`mcpServersUsed`/`toolProfile` separately)?
2. Add a per-row `—` with a tooltip-style reason on the labels row specifically when extraction is missing?
3. Land the local fallback for tool-time + skills in the CLI (independent of server state)?

Everything's wired. Here's how to test end-to-end:

## Test plan

**1. Start the API dev server from the recap-endpoint worktree** (separate terminal):

```bash
cd /Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/entire.io/.worktrees/recap-endpoint/api
pnpm dev
```

Wrangler dev runs on `http://localhost:8787` by default. If you prefer `--remote` mode so it uses real data, `pnpm dev:remote` instead.

**2. In this CLI worktree, point at the local API + run recap:**

```bash
ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787 ./entire recap --insecure-http-auth --week
```

- `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` overrides the production `https://entire.io`
- `--insecure-http-auth` bypasses the https-only guard for localhost
- `--refresh` also works to wipe the analysis cache if needed

**3. What to look for:**

- Agents card has skills/MCP/tool-mix populated on the **me** column (from deterministic parse, doesn't need LLM)
- When the repo has multiple contributors, the **contributors** column shows the same shape aggregated across everyone
- `transcriptTokens` and `filesChanged` land as new rows (aggregator now tracks them — though the renderer doesn't surface them yet, the JSON will show them)

TOKEN=$(entire status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r .token 2>/dev/null || echo "GET_FROM_KEYCHAIN")

1	# Entire Activity Design
2	
3	Date: 2026-04-15 (revised 2026-04-16)
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	`entire activity` is a new read-only product surface for understanding work captured by Entire over time.
8	
9	It is centered on:
10	
11	- **sessions** as the primary unit of work
12	- **checkpoints** as the evidence trail inside a session
13	- **repo, time, and agent** as first-class grouping dimensions
14	
15	This is not a sprint tool and should not use sprint language. It is an Entire-native activity layer over existing session, checkpoint, transcript, and commit-linkage data — rendered as a tabbed dashboard in the terminal.
16	
17	## Goals
18	
19	- Show what happened today and across selectable time ranges.
20	- Make checkpoint and session activity easy to scan quickly.
21	- Surface useful, defensible insights instead of generic churn metrics.
22	- Support today / range / history / agents / repos / report tabs in v1.
23	- Support interactive TUI and static output in v1.
24	- Use only metrics that are directly available now or safely derivable from existing data.
25	- Reuse existing CLI infrastructure (session state, checkpoint store, auth, lipgloss styles) rather than duplicating it.
26	
27	## Non-Goals
28	
29	- No productivity score.
30	- No “most modified files” leaderboard as a primary signal.
31	- No sprint framing.
32	- No LLM-generated prose in the CLI. (Server-side LLM classification is consumed as data, not re-generated locally.)
33	- No claims of labor time or focus time beyond actual timestamp spans.
34	- No local reimplementation of the server-side checkpoint analysis pipeline.
35	
36	## Product Definition
37	
38	`entire activity` answers:
39	
40	- what happened
41	- when it happened
42	- where it happened
43	- what kind of work it was
44	- which agents and models were involved
45	- which checkpoints linked to commits
46	- what should likely be resumed or finished
47	
48	## Information Architecture
49	
50	The v1 surface is a **tabbed dashboard**. Six top-level tabs:
51	
52	```
53	today │ range │ history │ agents │ repos │ report
54	```
55	
56	Rules:
57	
58	- Each tab is a self-contained view with its own panel layout. Panels never span tabs.
59	- Active tab is visually distinct (amber `214` with an underline rule); inactive tabs are faint gray `244`.
60	- Keyboard: `1-6` jump directly to a tab. `tab` / `shift-tab` cycle. `q` quits.
61	- Within a tab, arrow keys move between panels/rows. `enter` opens drill-down. `esc` closes drill-down.
62	- CLI subcommands map 1:1 to tabs: `entire activity today` opens the today tab, `entire activity agents` opens agents tab, etc.
63	
64	Profiles only change defaults and emphasis (heatmap metric, whether token panels are prominent, etc.):
65	
66	- `personal` (default)
67	- `team`
68	- `observability`
69	
70	## Command Surface
71	
72	```bash
73	entire activity                                 # opens TUI on 'today' tab
74	entire activity today
75	entire activity range --last 7d
76	entire activity range --from 2026-04-01 --to 2026-04-15
77	entire activity history
78	entire activity agents
79	entire activity repos
80	entire activity report --template daily --format markdown
81	```
82	
83	Shared flags:
84	
85	```bash
86	--repo current|owner/name|all|local
87	--profile personal|team|observability
88	--from YYYY-MM-DD
89	--to YYYY-MM-DD
90	--last 7d|14d|30d
91	--group-by repo|day|agent
92	--view cards|table
93	--json
94	--local-only    # never call the api; labels unavailable
95	--no-color      # also honors NO_COLOR env var
96	```
97	
98	Notes:
99	
100	- `entire activity` (no args) opens the TUI on the `today` tab.
101	- `--repo all` is the default for logged-in users and covers every repo the user has api access to. `--repo current` narrows to the current worktree's repo. `--repo local` forces offline / this-repo-only mode.
102	- All subcommands support static terminal output and JSON output.
103	- `--json` output always includes `"schema_version": "v1"` at the top level.
104	
105	## Execution Model
106	
107	### Local-first, api-enriched
108	
109	- **Local is the default data source.** `entire activity today` with no login returns a complete, honest view of the current repo's activity using only local data.
110	- **API enrichment is lazy.** When `entire login` has produced a token, the CLI fetches server-authoritative labels and tool-time data per checkpoint. Enrichment fills in asynchronously in the TUI and is batched before final print in static mode.
111	- **Offline / not-logged-in fallback** is silent. Tab chrome shows a single line: `labels: offline · tip: run 'entire login' for agent insights`.
112	- **Performance budget:**
113	  - `today`: < 1s local, < 2s with api enrichment
114	  - `range --last 7d`: < 3s local, < 6s with enrichment
115	  - `range --last 30d`: < 6s local, < 12s with enrichment
116	  - `history` (90d): < 10s local, < 30s with enrichment
117	- **Cache** at `.git/entire-activity-cache/<checkpoint-id>.json` for api responses. Invalidated when `StoredCheckpointAnalysis.pipeline_version` changes.
118	
119	### Three-tier Data Truth Table
120	
121	Every metric is sourced from exactly one tier. The UI tags metrics with their tier via the tab chrome footer (e.g. `labels: server · span: local · linked commits: local`).
122	
123	#### Tier 1 — Local-authoritative
124	
125	Readable from `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` (session state) and `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch (committed metadata):
126	
127	- session ID, checkpoint ID
128	- session started / ended / last-interaction timestamps
129	- session phase, step count
130	- checkpoint timestamps
131	- files touched per session / per checkpoint
132	- base commit, worktree path, worktree ID
133	- agent type, model name (when state records it)
134	- token usage (when the agent or hook reports it)
135	- prompt text (scoped per checkpoint)
136	- attribution metadata (`InitialAttribution`)

141	
142	Cheap computation from tier 1 with no api call:
143	
144	- **session span minutes** = `last_checkpoint_ts − first_checkpoint_ts` (honest first-to-last timestamp, replaces the FE `max(steps) × 2 / 60` estimate)
145	- checkpoints per session, checkpoint density, median checkpoint gap
146	- sessions/day, checkpoints/day
147	- active day count, streaks (same algorithm as FE `useUserDashboardData.ts`)
148	- heatmap cell intensity
149	- intra-day hour buckets
150	- resume-after-gap detection
151	- focus area assignment from `files_touched` via rule engine
152	- linked commit count, linked commit rate (via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer lookup)
153	- commit-linked vs exploratory-only split
154	- badges (`resumed`, `linked commit`, `delegated`, `multi-repo`)
155	- active-session rollups (un-pushed work that only exists locally)

157	#### Tier 3 — Server-authoritative
158	
159	Requires `entire login` and a network round trip. Fetched per committed checkpoint and cached:
160	
161	- **work-mode labels** — `CheckpointExtraction.labels[]` from `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` (18-value multi-label taxonomy, max 3 per checkpoint)
162	- **`toolProfile.categories[*].count`** — tool usage counts (shell / fileOps / search / mcp / agent / other)
163	- **`toolProfile.categories[*].durationMs`** — tool time per category (**pending upstream server change**, see Upstream Dependencies)
164	- `skillsUsed`, `mcpServersUsed`, `modelsUsed`, `agentsUsed`
165	- execution feedback: `thrashing`, `bugProfile`, `architectureChanges`
166	- cross-repo aggregation for `--repo all`
167	- session span canonicalization (**pending** — until then CLI uses tier 2)

170	
171	Activity types are **read-only projections**, not new primitives. They are built in `load.go` from existing `session.State` + `checkpoint.CheckpointSummary` + `checkpoint.CommittedMetadata` (+ optional api `StoredCheckpointAnalysis`). They are never persisted. The existing `session` and `checkpoint` packages remain the canonical owners of underlying data.

220	## Labels — Server-Authoritative
221	
222	### Why No Local Classifier
223	
224	The entire.io api already runs `checkpoint-analysis-pipeline.ts` (pipeline version `2026-04-10.v3`) which uses the Anthropic SDK to produce `CheckpointExtraction { labels[], blocks[] }`. Results are stored as `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` in the db. This is the same pipeline that drives the web app's checkpoint summary UI (PR #1021).
225	
226	A second classifier in the CLI would produce a different taxonomy, different weights, and eventual drift. Users would see `build` in the TUI and `feature_build` in the web app for the same checkpoint — a reportable bug. We avoid that by letting the server own classification and having the CLI consume and render.
227	
228	### Canonical Taxonomy
229	
230	Labels are multi-label with max 3 per checkpoint, drawn from `CHECKPOINT_LABELS` in `api/src/types.ts`:
231	
232	```
233	feature_build, bug_fix, refactor, performance, optimization,
234	investigation, configuration, testing, deployment, recovery,
235	planning, security_fix, documentation, migration, telemetry,
236	observability, enhancement, dependencies
237	```
238	
239	### Rendering
240	
241	- Session cards and checkpoint rows show up to 3 label pills (semantic color per label; see Visual Language).
242	- Sessions without a server analysis render **unlabeled**, not as `mixed`. Offline mode suppresses label pills entirely and notes it in the chrome footer.
243	- Range-level "modes" panels aggregate by summing label occurrences across checkpoints/sessions.
244	- A range never claims a dominant mode unless: top label share ≥ 0.55 and top leads runner-up by ≥ 0.15. Otherwise render `Modes: feature_build 4 · bug_fix 3 · testing 2`.
245	
246	## Badges — Local Deterministic
247	
248	Badges are cheap local facts, not classifications. They don't require the api.
249	
250	- `⚑ linked` — session has at least one `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer on an active-branch commit
251	- `↻ resumed` — session started after ≥ 6h gap from the prior session on the same branch
252	- `⇢ delegated` — session has task checkpoint count ≥ 1
253	- `◎ multi-repo` — session spans multiple repos (only available with `--repo all`)
254	- `● active` — session phase is `ACTIVE` or `IDLE` with `EndedAt == nil`
255	- `✓ committed` — checkpoint has a linked commit

257	## Tool Time — Agent Insights
258	
259	Tool-time breakdown is the primary metric on the `agents` tab. It answers "how much time did the agent spend grepping vs conversing vs committing."
260	
261	### Categories
262	
263	8 categories, semantically colored:
264	
265	| Category | Mapping rule | Color (256) |
266	|---|---|---|
267	| `shell` | `Bash` | `179` |
268	| `fileOps` | `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | `75` |
269	| `search` | `Grep`, `Glob` | `81` |
270	| `mcp` | `mcp__*` | `170` |
271	| `agent` | `Agent`, `Skill` | `99` |
272	| `other` | everything else | `244` |
273	| `conversation` | assistant text time between tool_result and next tool_use | `250` |
274	| `commit` | `Bash` where command matches `^git (commit\|push)` | `220` |
275	
276	`conversation` and `commit` are virtual categories:
277	
278	- `conversation` is a **sum of gaps** where the assistant produced text between a `tool_result` and the next `tool_use`. It does not overlap with any other category.
279	- `commit` is a **sub-bucket of shell**. Rendered as a secondary line under shell and summed separately ("of which committing: 6m"); not double-counted when categories are summed.
280	
281	### Derivation
282	
283	For each assistant message containing `tool_use` content blocks, measure timestamps from the transcript JSONL:
284	
285	```
286	duration(tool_use_i) = timestamp(next tool_use OR turn end) − timestamp(tool_use_i)
287	```
288	
289	For `conversation`:
290	
291	```
292	conversation_i = timestamp(next tool_use) − timestamp(tool_result_i)
293	                  counted only when assistant text was produced in the gap
294	```
295	
296	### Where Computation Lives
297	
298	- **For committed checkpoints** (tier 3): computed server-side by extending `extractToolMetrics` in `api/src/lib/analysis-queue.ts`. CLI consumes `toolProfile.categories[*].durationMs` from the api.
299	- **For active / un-pushed sessions** (tier 2): computed locally in the CLI by parsing the live transcript. Same algorithm, Go implementation, so the CLI can show tool-time for today's work before it's pushed.
300	
301	Honest labels: the UI calls this "Time between tool calls" or "Session time by category." Not "execution time" — it includes agent thinking.

317	## Focus Areas
318	
319	Focus areas are a required product signal. They determine which work clusters the user is spending time on.
320	
321	### Rule Source
322	
323	Resolution order:
324	
325	1. repo-local config (`.entire/activity_areas.json`)
326	2. built-in rules (shipped with the CLI)
327	3. fallback path clustering (first meaningful repo-relative directory boundary)
328	
329	Repo-local config schema:
330	
331	```json
332	{
333	  "version": 1,
334	  "areas": [
335	    { "match": "cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/**", "label": "checkpoint storage", "priority": 100 }
336	  ]
337	}
338	```
339	
340	### Matching Rules
341	
342	- highest priority wins
343	- ties broken by longest match
344	- fallback to first meaningful repo-relative directory boundary if no rule matches
345	
346	### Built-In Default Rules
347	
348	For this repo (entireio/cli):
349	
350	- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/**` → `checkpoint storage`
351	- `cmd/entire/cli/session/**` → `session state`
352	- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/**` → `checkpoint strategy`
353	- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/**` → `agent integrations`
354	- `cmd/entire/cli/search**` → `search`
355	- `cmd/entire/cli/explain**` → `explain`
356	- `cmd/entire/cli/status**` → `status`
357	- `cmd/entire/cli/activity/**` → `activity`
358	- `cmd/entire/cli/trail/**` → `trails`
359	- `cmd/entire/cli/hooks**` → `hooks`
360	- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/**` → `integration tests`
361	- `e2e/**` → `e2e`
362	- `docs/architecture/**` → `architecture docs`
363	- `docs/**` → `docs`
364	
365	### Area Ranking
366	
367	Do not rank by file count.
368	
369	Session area score:
370	
371	- `4 × checkpoint_participation`
372	- `+1` if area appears in 2+ consecutive checkpoints
373	- `+1` if area appears in a linked-commit session
374	
375	Range area score:
376	
377	- `3 × session_participation`
378	- `3 × checkpoint_participation`
379	- `+1` if area appears across multiple repos (only with `--repo all`)
380	
381	Render only top 1–3 focus areas in summary surfaces.

760	- `static.go` — static renderer for non-tty / piped
761	- `json.go` — JSON output with `schema_version: "v1"`
762	- `report.go` — daily/weekly markdown templates

764	CLI entrypoints (thin wrappers over the package):
765	
766	- `cmd/entire/cli/activity.go` — root + today (default)

771	- `cmd/entire/cli/activity_report.go`

773	Small shared refactor:
774	
775	- Extract `timeAgo` from `status.go` into `stringutil/time.go` so `activity` + `status` + `sessions` all share it.
776	
777	## JSON Output
778	
779	Every `--json` response:
780	
781	```json
782	{
783	  "schema_version": "v1",
784	  "generated_at": "2026-04-16T14:23:11Z",
785	  "scope": { "repo": "entireio/cli", "from": "2026-04-09", "to": "2026-04-16" },
786	  "sessions": [ ... ],
787	  "aggregates": { ... }
788	}
789	```
790	
791	Schema versioning makes the output a stable contract. Downstream tools gate on `schema_version` before parsing.
792	
793	## Validation Plan
794	
795	### Data projection
796	
797	- Unit tests for `load.go` using in-memory fake session states and committed metadata. Assert the resulting `ActivitySession` fields match expectations.
798	- Table-driven tests for focus-area rule matching: priority, longest-match, fallback.
799	- Tests for `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer lookup against fixture git repos (use `testutil.InitRepo`).
800	
801	### Metrics
802	
803	- Session-span derivation across edge cases: single checkpoint, identical timestamps, missing timestamps.
804	- Heatmap bucketing across timezones.
805	- Streak calculation on sparse date sets (matches FE `useUserDashboardData.ts` behavior).
806	- Linked-commit rate with and without trailers.
807	
808	### Api enrichment
809	
810	- Mock `api.Client` returning `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` stubs.
811	- Cache hit / miss paths.
812	- Offline fallback: ensure no api calls when no token present.
813	- Pipeline version invalidation.
814	
815	### TUI
816	
817	- Snapshot tests for each tab's panel rendering at 80, 100, 160 cols.
818	- View switching, drill-down state, `ACCESSIBLE=1` fallback path.
819	
820	### Golden output
821	
822	- `--json` golden files per tab, frozen clock.
823	- Static renderer golden files per tab with `NO_COLOR=1`.
824	
825	## Risks
826	
827	- `--repo all` requires api access; offline users get single-repo only. Documented in `labels: offline · tip: ...` footer.
828	- Tool-time measurements include agent thinking (not pure exec time). Label explicitly as "Time between tool calls."
829	- Commit-link lookup across long ranges can be slow. Mitigated by caching and lazy enrichment.
830	- Weak focus-area rules produce noisy summaries. Mitigated by repo-local `.entire/activity_areas.json` override.
831	- Dashboard density at 80 cols — narrow-mode stacked layout handles this.
832	
833	## Decisions (Locked)
834	
835	- Tabbed dashboard-first UI with 6 tabs.
836	- Local-first data model with lazy api enrichment; three-tier truth table.
837	- Sessions as containers, checkpoints as evidence; activity types are projections, never persisted.
838	- Repo is a first-class dimension; `--repo all` is default for logged-in users.
839	- No sprint framing, no file-churn leaderboard, no LLM prose in CLI.
840	- Server-authoritative labels via `StoredCheckpointAnalysis` (18-label multi-label taxonomy); no local classifier.
841	- Honest session span time via first-to-last checkpoint timestamp.
842	- Tool-time breakdown with 8 categories (6 tool + conversation + commit).
843	- Drill-down surfaces real `entire ...` commands as an Actions footer.
844	- `--json` includes `schema_version: "v1"` from day one.
845	- Visual language inherits lipgloss palette, extends with semantic label colors and per-panel borders.
846	- No emoji — Unicode geometry only.
847	- Upstream server changes (durationMs, session_span_ms) are optional enrichment, not v1 blockers.

# Entire Activity Replan

Date: 2026-04-21
Supersedes: `docs/2026-04-15-entire-activity-design.md` (6-tab, local-aggregation design)

## Premise

Two server endpoints now cover 90% of what `entire activity` needs to show:

- `GET /api/v1/me/activity` — stats, `daily_contributions`, `hourly_contributions`, repo breakdown (PR #1590 landed)
- `GET /api/v1/me/recap` — per-agent checkpoints / tokens / labels / skills / mcpServers / toolMix, with optional contributors column when `?repo=` is set (in review on `feat/me-recap-endpoint`)

Everything else is already local: session state (`.git/entire-sessions/`), checkpoints (`entire/checkpoints/v1`), tool-time walker (commits `7560cd2…646625fc`). The CLI is a renderer, not an aggregator.

Replan goal: collapse the old 6-tab dashboard into **3 tabs** that map 1:1 to those data sources, and delete the local-aggregation code it obsoletes.

## Non-Goals

- No new server endpoints. If a metric isn't in `/me/activity` or `/me/recap`, cut it.
- No local classifier, no focus-area rule engine, no heatmap binning in the CLI. Charts render what the server sends.
- No `report` / `history` tabs in v1. Postpone.
- No rename back to `activity/` package yet — the package stays `recap/` until the command is renamed in Chunk 3.

## Three Tabs

| Tab | Source | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **overview** | `GET /me/activity` | KPI bar (sessions, checkpoints, linked, streak), 7-day bar, 24-hour strip, active-sessions tail (local) |
| **agents** | `GET /me/recap` + local tool-time | Per-agent row: checkpoints, tokens, top labels, top skills, toolMix bars, `of which committing:` |
| **repos** | `/me/activity.repos` | Per-repo card: total + per-agent contribution counts |

Keyboard: `1/2/3` jump, `tab`/`shift-tab` cycle, `←/→` range (day/week/30d/90d), `q` quits. Range selector lives in the header, not per-tab.

## Data Flow

```
entire activity
  └── fetchMeActivity(timeframe, tz)  ─┐
  └── fetchMeRecap(timeframe, repo)   ─┤── one model ─> three tab renderers
  └── localActiveSessions()           ─┘
```

- Both server calls run in parallel from the bubbletea `Init` command.
- Local active-session scan is synchronous (cheap) — used only on the overview tab for un-pushed work.
- Tool-time for active sessions uses the per-agent `WalkToolCalls` walkers (already merged); committed-checkpoint tool-time comes from `toolMix` on the recap response.
- No cache layer in v1. Endpoints are cheap; reopening the TUI re-fetches. Cache can come later if measured.

## Scope Cuts (vs. 2026-04-15 design)

Delete or skip:

- `recap/heatmap.go` — 7-day bar and 24-hour strip render from `daily_contributions` / `hourly_contributions` directly; no binning needed.
- `recap/badges.go` — badges were a tier-2 local derivation. Keep `● active` only; cut the rest.
- `recap/insights.go` — "dominant mode" gating logic belongs server-side if at all.
- Six-tab TUI → three-tab TUI. Drill-down overlay postponed.
- `cmd/entire/cli/activity_{range,history,agents,repos,report}.go` entrypoints — one binary, `entire activity`.
- `--profile personal|team|observability` flag — unused in a 3-tab view.
- `--json` schema_version — keep, but only for overview+agents. Repos tab is a subset.

Keep:

- `recap/load.go`, `load_linked.go`, `load_checkpoints.go` — active-session rollup for overview's tail.
- `recap/styles.go`, `render_chart.go`, `render_panel.go` — visual primitives.
- `recap/agents_card.go` — already wired for me + contributors columns.
- `recap/me_recap.go` — the client for `/me/recap`.

## File Structure

| File | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd/entire/cli/activity.go` | Cobra entrypoint, flag parsing, TUI launch | **new** (replaces `recap.go` once we're confident) |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/me_activity.go` | Client for `GET /me/activity` (mirrors `me_recap.go`) | **new** |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/tui.go` | 3-tab bubbletea model | **rewrite** (currently single-view) |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/overview_panel.go` | KPI row + 7-day bar + 24h strip + active tail | **new** |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/repos_panel.go` | Repo card list | **new** |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/agents_card.go` | Per-agent rows | keep |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/render_chart.go` | Bars + strips | keep |
| `cmd/entire/cli/recap/{heatmap,insights,badges}.go` | Local aggregation | **delete** |

Package rename (`recap/` → `activity/`) is a separate PR after the command flips.

## Chunks

### Chunk 1: Server client for `/me/activity`

- Add `cmd/entire/cli/recap/me_activity.go` — `FetchMeActivity(ctx, client, timeframe, tz, limit) (*ActivityResponse, error)` mirroring the shape in `api/src/routes/me.ts:133-163`.
- Tests against a `httptest.Server` returning golden JSON from the endpoint's zod schema.
- Commit: `feat(activity): client for GET /me/activity`.

### Chunk 2: 3-tab TUI shell

- Rewrite `recap/tui.go` — `type model struct { tab int; overview, agents, repos *tabState; range_ RangeKey }`.
- Wire `1/2/3`, `tab`, `←/→`, `q`. Header shows range + timeframe + loading spinner per tab.
- Skeleton panel files return placeholder text; fetch commands dispatch both endpoints in parallel.
- Commit: `feat(activity): 3-tab TUI shell with parallel fetch`.

### Chunk 3: Overview panel

- KPI row from `response.stats` (tasks, orchestration, iteration, throughput, streak, current_streak).
- 7-day bar aggregating `daily_contributions` server-side (already summed per agent); render with the existing `render_chart.go` gradient bar.
- 24-hour strip from `hourly_contributions` keyed to local tz (the endpoint already bucketed in the caller-supplied tz).
- Active-sessions tail: reuse `recap/load.go` for un-pushed sessions only; 3-row limit.
- Commit: `feat(activity): overview tab`.

### Chunk 4: Agents panel

- Consume `/me/recap` response; render one row per agent via `agents_card.go`.
- Overlay local tool-time for active sessions (WalkToolCalls walkers) onto the "me" column; contributors column is server-only.
- Commit: `feat(activity): agents tab wired to /me/recap`.

### Chunk 5: Repos panel

- Consume `response.repos` from `/me/activity`. One card per repo: total count + 3 top agent counts.
- No drill-down; selecting a repo later can narrow `/me/recap?repo=` — postpone.
- Commit: `feat(activity): repos tab`.

### Chunk 6: Command rename + cleanup

- Add `entire activity` cobra command; keep `entire recap` as a hidden alias for one release.
- Delete `recap/{heatmap,insights,badges}.go` + tests.
- Update `--help`, README snippet, e2e canary prompts.
- Commit: `feat(activity): rename entire recap to entire activity`.

## Testing

- Unit: each fetch client against `httptest.Server`. Each panel against a frozen response fixture (golden string assertion at 80/120 col widths).
- Integration: `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/` — run `entire activity --json` against a mock server, assert `schema_version: "v1"` and shape.
- E2E: no new canary — the Vogon agent doesn't exercise network endpoints. Manual smoke: `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787 entire activity --insecure-http-auth`.

## Risks

- `/me/recap` hasn't merged yet. Chunk 4 blocks on that PR. Chunks 1-3 can land independently.
- `hourly_contributions` is bucketed in a caller-supplied tz; the CLI must pass the user's IANA tz (`time.Local.String()` gives it on most systems). Fall back to `UTC` with a footer note.
- Deleting `heatmap.go` removes the 90-day grid. If the server later grows a `/me/activity/heatmap` endpoint, re-add as a 4th tab, not inline.

## Open Questions (non-blocking)

- Should the range selector push `timeframe=` to both endpoints, or let each tab set its own? **Propose:** single global range, refetch both on change.
- Do we want a `--repo=current` filter in v1? **Propose:** yes — `/me/recap?repo=` already supports it; `/me/activity` does not, so the repos tab stays cross-repo.
- Is `recap` package rename worth a dedicated PR? **Propose:** yes, after Chunk 6, to keep diffs reviewable.

```bash

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`go-keyring` (the Go library the CLI uses) base64-wraps keychain values whenever the stored string contains characters the Keychain Services API would mangle — non-ASCII bytes or NULs. The Go library strips the prefix and base64-decodes on read; anything else calling the keychain has to do the same dance. This is why `LookupCurrentToken()` "just works" from inside the CLI but `security -w` feels broken.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Diagnosed. The 401 isn't the token format — it's that your `ent_...` token is in the **production** D1 database, but wrangler dev uses a **local** D1 at `.wrangler/state/v3/d1/`. The middleware does `db.apiTokens.findByTokenHash(sha256(token))` (line 196) and the local DB has zero rows, so the lookup fails at line 199 → "Not authenticated."

Two paths forward — pick whichever matches your intent:

### Path A — seed a token into local D1 (fastest to test)

Hash your prod token and insert a row so the local DB recognizes it. Paste in a second fish tab (wrangler stays running):

```fish
set RAW (security find-generic-password -s entire-cli -a "https://entire.io" -w)
set TOKEN (string replace "go-keyring-base64:" "" -- $RAW | base64 -d)
set HASH (echo -n $TOKEN | shasum -a 256 | awk '{print $1}')
echo "Token hash: $HASH"
```

Then in the same terminal, from `/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/entire.io/.worktrees/recap-endpoint/api`:

```fish
cd /Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/entire.io/.worktrees/recap-endpoint/api
# First: find your user_id in local D1 (or seed one)
bunx wrangler d1 execute entireio-db --local --command "SELECT id FROM users LIMIT 1"
# Then insert the api_token row with the hash above and that user_id
bunx wrangler d1 execute entireio-db --local --command "INSERT INTO api_tokens (id, user_id, token_hash, name, expires_at, created_at) VALUES ('dev-1', '<user-id-from-above>', '<HASH>', 'local-dev', datetime('now', '+1 year'), datetime('now'))"
```

If the local users table is empty, this won't work — you need at least one user row. That means Path B.

### Path B — log in against localhost (recommended, tests the full stack)

```fish
cd /Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/entire-activity
env ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787 go run ./cmd/entire login --insecure-http-auth
```

This runs the device-auth flow against your local wrangler, which walks through OAuth to GitHub, creates a user row in local D1, and writes a new token keyed to `http://localhost:8787` in your keychain. After that:

```fish
env ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787 go run ./cmd/entire recap --insecure-http-auth --week --repo entireio/cli
```

will hit `/me/recap` with a valid local token — proving the endpoint end-to-end.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is a common gotcha with Cloudflare Workers local dev: `.dev.vars` gives you secrets that match prod, but **bindings** (D1, KV, Durable Objects, R2) are locally simulated by default. So JWT-signed stuff works cross-environment, but anything backed by a binding query (which is the majority of auth checks) needs fresh local data. It's why `wrangler dev --remote` exists — that flag points at real prod bindings, but you almost never want that for development.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

My recommendation: **Path B**. It tests the actual flow a user hits and populates local D1 in the process, which you'll need for iterating on the endpoint anyway.

**1. `entireio/cli` has zero local checkpoints.** The 5 rows in your local DB are:

```

```

Filtering to `?repo=entireio/cli` correctly returns 0 — there's nothing there to aggregate.

**2. Me-side tokens are intentionally omitted by design.** Line 6 of the endpoint I wrote says `(tokens intentionally omitted — the CLI sums metadata.json locally)`. The 14243 input_tokens on Gemini are in the DB, just not exposed on the me side of this endpoint — the CLI already has better token counts from local metadata.

**3. `repo_checkpoint_analyses` table doesn't exist in local dev.** Checked `db/init-test-db.sql` — it's not in the schema, so when the aggregator queries for labels/skills/mcpServers/toolMix, it gets nothing. This is a local-dev limitation; production PlanetScale has it.

content.text:
500 on the repo-scoped path — the contributors side calls `db.repoOverview.getAgentActivityDaily(...)` which hits more tables that don't exist locally (the same schema gap as `repo_checkpoint_analyses`). The endpoint code is correct; the local MySQL is a subset of prod.

**Where that leaves us:**

| Path | Local result | Production expected |
|---|---|---|
| `?timeframe=last-6-months` (no repo) | ✅ 4 agents with checkpoint counts | Full data including analyses |
| `?repo=test-entire-local` (contributors path) | ❌ 500 (missing `repo_checkpoint_analyses`) | Full contributor aggregates |

The green signal from path 1 is what matters — it proved: auth works, routing works, `meRoutes.route("/recap", recapRoutes)` mount is correct, zod schema matches response, aggregator runs without error, checkpoint counts aggregate by agent. The enrichment fields (labels/skills/tokens/filesChanged/toolMix) are dark locally by design — three-tier schema: local dev has rows, prod has rows + analyses + pre-computed aggregates.

**Recommendation:** commit the three files and open the PR against entire.io. The full-data smoke test happens after merge on the deploy preview or staging, where the analyses table is populated. Continuing to hammer this locally means either (a) seeding `repo_checkpoint_analyses` manually with fake JSON blobs, or (b) pointing wrangler at prod with `--remote`, which risks writes — neither is worth it for a read-only endpoint.

Want me to:

1. Run `pnpm --filter entire-api check` (or whatever the test task is) first, then commit + PR?
2. Just commit + PR directly with a good message?
3. Hold off — you want to seed fake analyses data so you can see the full-lit response locally first?

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is the classic "local dev uses a reduced schema" trap in Cloudflare Workers projects that front PlanetScale. PlanetScale schema lives in its own control plane (branches + deploy requests), not in migration files checked into the repo — so the local Docker MySQL only mirrors whatever someone manually captured in `init-test-db.sql`, which drifts behind production. You'll see this recur: whenever a PR touches a table that was added to PlanetScale but never backported to `init-test-db.sql`, local dev silently returns empty or 500s while prod works fine.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
is this one just for tokens?

No — tokens is 1 of 8 fields on each side. Per agent, per side (me / contributors), the endpoint returns:

| Field | Source | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| `checkpoints` | `repo_checkpoints` row count | deterministic |
| `transcriptTokens` | sum of transcript token counts | deterministic |
| `filesChanged` | sum from `repo_commits.files_changed` | deterministic |
| `tokens` | contributors only (me side is intentionally 0) | deterministic |
| `labels` | `CheckpointExtraction.labels[]` from analyses | LLM-dependent |
| `skills` | `skillsUsed` from analyses | LLM-dependent |
| `mcpServers` | `mcpServersUsed` from analyses | LLM-dependent |
| `toolMix` | `toolProfile.categories` from analyses | LLM-dependent |

The top 4 survive with the LLM pipeline off. The bottom 4 require `repo_checkpoint_analyses` to be populated (which is why they're empty locally).

So the endpoint's real job is **one call replaces three**:
- `GET /me/checkpoints` (list)
- `POST /checkpoints/analyses/batch` (per-checkpoint analyses)
- `GET /:org/:repo/overview/*` (contributor rollup)

…and it stitches per-agent on the server instead of making the CLI do client-side joining. Tokens is just one dimension of that; it's listed in the payload but the design note says the CLI should overwrite it from local metadata, so in practice it's noise in the me-side response.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The reason tokens sits in the payload at all is pure schema symmetry: same shape on me and contributors sides keeps the CLI rendering code uniform. If we dropped `tokens` from me, the CLI would need a conditional render — "if contributors, show tokens column; if me, hide it." Symmetry costs a zeroed field; asymmetry costs a branch in every renderer. The 8-field payload chose symmetry, and the `(tokens intentionally omitted)` comment documents that tradeoff so future readers don't assume the field is broken.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

If you were hoping for a different metric we don't have yet — e.g. turn count, session span, heatmap bucketing — that'd be a follow-up endpoint, not a change to `/me/recap`.

**End-to-end working.** The CLI now renders real per-agent data with me/contributors columns side by side:

- **Claude Code**: me = 15 sessions / 92 checkpoints / 2.9M tokens (local), contributors = 2 checkpoints / bug_fix+feature_build+refactor labels / code-simplifier+session-handoff+using-superpowers skills / linear-server MCP / fileOps 61% · search 18% · shell 15% tool mix (server) ✅
- **Codex**: me = 24 sessions / 647k tokens (local only — Codex wasn't in seed data so contributors is `—`) ✅

This proves the whole round-trip:

| Stage | Verified |
|---|---|
| Keychain → bearer header | ✅ 200 OK |
| Middleware validates `ent_...` tokens against local DB | ✅ |
| `/me/recap` aggregator runs, queries `repo_checkpoint_analyses` | ✅ |
| JSON response matches zod schema | ✅ |
| Go client `FetchMeRecap` parses response | ✅ |
| `ContributorsFromMeRecap` converts to `ContributorsData` | ✅ |
| `applyContributors` overlays onto agent cards | ✅ |
| Static renderer displays me/contributors columns | ✅ |

**One observation worth flagging** — the endpoint returns `me.labels/skills/mcpServers/toolMix` but the CLI's `ContributorsFromMeRecap` only extracts the *contributors* side. That's why the me column's label/skill cells show `—` even though the server sent data. This is an architectural choice (me column uses local-only data today), not a bug. If you want the me enrichment to flow through later, it'd be a follow-up PR on the CLI.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The CLI's rendering design — "me column is local, contributors is server" — means `/me/recap`'s `me` side is partially unused today. That's intentional: local session metadata is richer and more real-time than server aggregates for the caller's own work. The me-side fields in the endpoint are there to let future clients (web dashboard, programmatic integrations) get a complete picture in one call even when they don't have local sessions. content.text:
Here's the full picture. Two separate mechanisms drive the two columns:

| Column | Source | Why empty now |
|---|---|---|
| **me** (per-agent) | Per-checkpoint GET `/api/v1/cache/<repo>/checkpoints/<id>/analysis` | Your 92 local Claude Code checkpoint IDs don't match the 5 I seeded — each lookup returns 404 / incomplete → silently skipped |
| **contributors** (per-agent) | New `/api/v1/me/recap` aggregate | Populated for 4 agents I seeded, empty for Codex (didn't seed it) |

### Why me labels/skills/MCP/toolMix are blank

The me side enriches each local checkpoint by calling:

```
GET /api/v1/cache/entireio/cli/checkpoints/<checkpoint-id>/analysis
```

Per checkpoint. See `enrich.go:79-95`. It **needs a server-side analysis row keyed to that exact checkpoint_id**. My 5 seeded rows use checkpoint_ids like `f11ed66a2b62` (from the test-entire-local repo). Your local Claude Code sessions use different IDs — the 92 IDs in `.git/entire-sessions/*.json`. So every lookup is a miss.

In production this works fine because your local IDs match server IDs one-to-one (the CLI created them, the server analyzed them). In our local-dev seed, the IDs are disconnected.

### Why Codex contributors is also blank

I only seeded analyses for 4 agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode). No Codex rows in `repo_checkpoints` → Codex isn't in the `/me/recap` response → CLI renders `—`.

### Quick fix if you want all agents fully lit

Either:

**A — seed Codex** so contributors column shows it too:

```fish
docker exec api-mysql-1 mysql -u entire -pentire entire -e "
INSERT INTO repo_checkpoints (id, repo_id, checkpoint_id, agent, input_tokens, output_tokens, created_at, synced_at)
VALUES (UUID(), '019d6918-9a35-7614-b00a-0a7124620260', 'codex-seed-1', 'Codex', 1200, 800, NOW(), NOW());
INSERT INTO repo_checkpoint_analyses (id, repo_id, checkpoint_id, status, analysis_json, attempt_count, queued_at, started_at, completed_at)
VALUES (UUID(), '019d6918-9a35-7614-b00a-0a7124620260', 'codex-seed-1', 'complete',
  '{\"totalFilesChanged\":5,\"total_transcript_tokens\":3200,\"pipeline_version\":\"local-seed.v1\",\"extraction\":{\"labels\":[\"investigation\",\"refactor\"]},\"skillsUsed\":[\"codex:codex-rescue\"],\"mcpServersUsed\":[],\"toolProfile\":{\"categories\":{\"shell\":{\"count\":15},\"fileOps\":{\"count\":22},\"search\":{\"count\":9},\"mcp\":{\"count\":0},\"agent\":{\"count\":3},\"other\":{\"count\":1}},\"total\":50}}',
  1, NOW(), NOW(), NOW());
"
```

**B — for me-side enrichment**, we'd have to seed analyses with your actual local checkpoint IDs (expensive — 92 of them for Claude Code alone). Not worth for this smoke test. In production this won't be an issue because your committed checkpoints really do have server analyses at their IDs.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is the architectural trade-off the `/me/recap` endpoint was designed around: contributors-side labels/skills need a server aggregate (one call, many checkpoints), while me-side labels come from per-checkpoint lookups that the CLI already caches. The endpoint intentionally doesn't replace the me-side per-checkpoint fetcher — doing so would either double-fetch every checkpoint or drop the cache granularity that makes the enrichment fast across sessions. The `me.*` fields in the response exist so web dashboards (no local cache) get a complete one-call picture; the CLI sticks with per-checkpoint because caching pays off there.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Bottom line**: the two empty-ish patterns you're seeing are local-dev artifacts, not endpoint bugs. In production your me column will populate (your IDs match the server's) and every agent you've used will have contributors data (full pipeline analysis runs for all of them).

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec review loop** — dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent with precisely crafted review context (never your session history); fix issues and re-dispatch until approved (max 5 iterations, then surface to human)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot

    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];

    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";

    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];

    "Spec review passed?" -> "User reviews spec?" [label="approved"];

    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Review Loop:**
After writing the spec document:

1. Dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent (see spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md)
2. If Issues Found: fix, re-dispatch, repeat until Approved
3. If loop exceeds 5 iterations, surface to human for guidance

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

**Rules that make the bars sane across edge cases:**

- **Scale**: bar width fills the available column. `you` fills proportional to `max(you, team)`; `team` renders as an overlay dot pattern (`▒`) past where `you` ends (or before if team > you).
- **Zero handling**: if `you = 0` and `team > 0`, flip — team fills, you overlays. The side with more data always dominates visually.
- **Both zero**: row is dropped entirely (no point showing an empty metric).
- **Numeric readout**: always `you / team` on the right, human-formatted (`2.9M / 1k`, not `2901234 / 1045`).

**Three field groups, always in this order:**

1. **Comparison bars** — tokens, sessions, checkpoints. Always shown when at least one side has a non-zero value.
2. **Team qualitative fields** — labels, skills, tool mix. Prefixed `team` because they only come from server aggregates. Skipped if no team data.
3. **Your qualitative fields** — models, repos. Prefixed `your` because they only come from local data. Skipped if no me data.

**Empty = row disappears.** No more `—` placeholders. Agents that have zero data on a side just show fewer rows.

# Entire Recap — Visual Redesign Spec

**Date:** 2026-04-22
**Scope:** Visual redesign of `entire recap` (CLI) static + TUI output.
**Supersedes:** The existing layout in `cmd/entire/cli/recap/render_static.go` + per-card renderer in `recap/agents_card.go`.

## Goal

Make `entire recap` a polished daily-use surface. Users run it to see their own work and the team's work side by side, with a single keyboard toggle to focus on either side. The current layout has dead placeholder rows (`—`, `(mixed)`, `0 tokens · 0 commits`), awkward wraps on long skill/model lists, repeated column headers, and a bottom panel that duplicates content already in the agent cards. This spec replaces the layout with a tighter three-panel page and a new per-agent card built around visual comparison bars.

## Non-goals

- No new server endpoints. Everything below reads the existing `/api/v1/me/recap`, `/api/v1/cache/<repo>/checkpoints/<id>/analysis`, and local session state.
- No rename to `entire activity`. That's a separate follow-up spec (see `docs/2026-04-21-entire-activity-replan.md`).
- No change to time-range semantics or agent filter behavior beyond removing the `--30` flag.
- No change to `--json` or `--format` flags. Output schema stays stable.

## Page composition

Three panels, top-to-bottom, separated by one blank line:

1. **Summary panel** — range title, you/team metric split, `top` line, context line.
2. **Activity strip** — range-dependent heatmap.
3. **Agents panel** — one card per agent with data.

The bottom panel (worktrees · labels · repos) from the current layout is **removed**. Labels are already in agent cards (`team labels`), repos are already in agent cards (`your repos`), and worktrees adds no daily value.

A diagnostic note footer (`ℹ Labels require server analysis…`) renders below the Agents panel only when at least one card has pending analyses. Suppressed otherwise.

## Header bar

A single line at the top, three tab groups left-to-right:

```
  day · week · month · [90d]        agent: [all]        view: you · team · [both]
```

Rules:
- Active option wrapped in brackets and rendered in amber (`214`). Inactive in muted gray (`8` / `555`).
- Dots (`·`) separate options within a group.
- Roomy whitespace between groups so each reads as its own control.
- TUI: `1/2/3/4` jumps to day/week/month/90d. `v` cycles view: `you → team → both → you`. `a` opens agent filter. `q` quits.
- Static: corresponding `--day` / `--week` / `--month` / `--90`, `--view me|contributors|both`, `--<agent-name>` flags.

The **`--30` flag is removed.** `--month` (this calendar month) covers the same practical window without the redundancy. Update `render_static.go:renderHeader` to drop the `30d` tab option, and remove the flag from `recap.go`. If any user has `--30` muscle-memory, a deprecation shim isn't needed — the flag has never shipped to production (still on feature branch).

## Summary panel spec

```
╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Last 90 days                                                          │
│                                                                        │
│  you   40 sessions   92 checkpoints   3.5M tok                         │
│  team  5 sessions    6 checkpoints    17k tok                          │
│                                                                        │
│  top  Codex · code-simplifier · bug_fix · claude-opus-4-7[1m]          │
│                                                                        │
│  5 agents · 1 repo · 14 active days                                    │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Content rules:

- **Title line** — `Last 90 days` (or `Today`, `Last 7 days`, `This month`). Always renders. Rendered in amber.
- **you row / team row** — 3 metrics each, in fixed order: sessions, checkpoints, tokens. Both rows always render (even when one side is zero — the zero is meaningful: "no team activity").
- **Prefix columns** — `you` rendered in amber-bold, `team` rendered in magenta-bold (matching the per-agent card prefixes).
- **`top` line** — up to 4 signals in fixed order: top agent, top skill, top label, top model. Separator is ` · `.
  - Empty signals **omit** — the line reflows.
  - All four empty → the `top` line **doesn't render** at all.
  - Top agent uses agent's canonical color (amber). Top skill uses cyan. Top label uses the label's semantic color (bug_fix=red, feature_build=green, etc.). Top model uses value-emphasis (white-bold).
- **Context line** — `N agents · M repos · K active days`. Always renders when there's any data. Muted gray.

"Focus" is renamed to "top label" — same underlying data (the dominant label in the range), but the `(mixed)` sentinel is replaced by simply omitting the slot.

## Activity strip spec

```
Activity · 90d                                          most active: Apr 11
░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░▒░░░░▒░░░░░░░░░░░█▓░░░░█▓
Jan 24   Feb 7    Feb 21   Mar 7    Mar 21   Apr 4    Apr 18   Today
```

Rules:

- **Show every cell in range**, including zero-activity days. Zero days render as the darkest shade (`green-0` / `237`). Today's default only renders cells where activity exists, which makes ranges look broken.
- **Pad to full terminal width** so axis labels align under their cells.
- **Rightmost cell is always today**, leftmost is range start. Fixed anchoring.
- **Peak annotation** — `most active: <date>` top-right of the strip. Renders only when at least one day has non-zero activity. The peak is the day with max `you_sessions + team_sessions`.
- Intra-day (`--day`) and 7-day (`--week`) variants reuse the existing `renderIntraDayStrip` / day-of-week-initials label row in `render_static.go` — same padding rules apply there.

## Agents panel spec

The Agents panel header carries the comparison legend, so per-card headers are gone:

```
╭─ Agents · last 90 days ────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                you ███   team ▒            │
│                                                                            │
│ <agent cards here, separated by blank lines>                               │
│                                                                            │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

**Panel rules:**
- Title includes the range: `Agents · last 90 days`.
- Legend row appears once under the title when view is `both`. In `you` or `team` single views, the legend is omitted (the bar color tells you which side).
- Cards sorted by combined `you_sessions + team_sessions` descending.
- No pagination — show every agent with any data. Typical case is 2–6 agents.
- Empty panel: single line `(no agent activity in range)`, muted.

### Per-agent card (view: both)

```
Claude Code
  tokens       █████████████████████████████████▒  2.9M / 1k
  sessions     █████████████████████▒▒▒             15 / 2
  checkpoints  ██████████████████████████████▒      92 / 2

  team labels    ● bug_fix  ● feature_build  ● refactor
  team skills    code-simplifier, session-handoff, using-super…
  team tool mix  fileOps 61% · search 18% · shell 15%

  your models    claude-opus-4-7[1m], claude-opus-4-6[1m]
  your repos     entireio/cli (15)
```

**Card structure — three field groups in fixed order, separated by blank lines:**

1. **Comparison bars** — `tokens`, `sessions`, `checkpoints`.
   - Each row: label + bar + readout.
   - Bar total width is panel-relative (budget roughly half the panel's inner width).
   - Bar fill: the larger side fills proportionally to `max(you, team)`. The smaller side overlays as dot pattern (`▒`) extending to its proportional length.
   - If `you >= team`: amber fill up to `you_ratio × width`, then magenta dots up to `team_ratio × width`.
   - If `team > you`: flipped — magenta fill up to `team_ratio × width`, amber fill up to `you_ratio × width`.
   - Readout: `<you_value> / <team_value>`, human-formatted (`2.9M / 1k`, not `2901234 / 1045`). Use `formatTokens` for tokens; integers verbatim for sessions/checkpoints.
   - If a row has both sides zero, the **row drops entirely**. No `0 / 0` clutter.
   - If one side is nil (not zero — genuinely absent because the user isn't logged in or data hasn't synced), that side shows `—` in the readout but the bar renders as whatever data exists.
2. **Team qualitative fields** — `team labels`, `team skills`, `team tool mix`.
   - Prefixed `team` (magenta-bold label) when view is `both` to disambiguate source.
   - In view `team`, the prefix drops; the column header is implied.
   - In view `you`, this entire block is skipped (team fields have no you equivalent).
   - Block skipped when team has no analysis data.
   - Labels render with semantic per-label colors (existing palette in `styles.go`). Skills render in cyan. Tool mix renders plain.
   - Soft-truncate with `…` when the single-line content exceeds the inner panel width. Never wrap.
3. **Your qualitative fields** — `your models`, `your repos`.
   - Prefixed `your` (amber-bold label) when view is `both`.
   - In view `you`, prefix drops.
   - In view `team`, this entire block is skipped.
   - Block skipped when you have no local session data for this agent.

### Empty-row behavior (consolidated)

No `—` placeholder rows. The old design kept card shape consistent with `—` in every missing slot. The new design **drops rows** instead. Cards naturally expand or shrink to what's actually meaningful.

The only `—` that ever renders is **inside the readout** of a comparison bar, e.g. `647k / —`, when one side has a value and the other is nil. This is a single-glyph marker in a row that's already present for a reason.

### View toggle semantics

| Aspect | view: you | view: team | view: both (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bar color | amber fill only | magenta fill only | amber fill + magenta overlay |
| Bar scale | max of you values across agents | max of team values across agents | max(you, team) per row |
| Numeric readout | `<you>` | `<team>` | `<you> / <team>` |
| Qualitative rows | models, repos (no prefix) | labels, skills, tool mix (no prefix) | both groups with `your` / `team` prefix |
| Legend row | hidden | hidden | shown |
| Total card width | narrow (one column's worth) | narrow | wide |

Keyboard/flag:
- TUI: `v` cycles `you → team → both`.
- Static: `--view me|contributors|both` (flag names stay as-is for continuity with existing contract).

## Empty-state handling

- **No data at all in range** — panel renders with empty body lines. Summary shows `you  0 sessions  0 checkpoints  0 tok` + `team 0 …`. Activity strip renders the full cell grid at the zero shade. Agents panel shows `(no agent activity in range)`. No diagnostic note.
- **Not logged in** — me side renders from local data; team side shows `—` in readouts; legend/prefixes still explain the split. Diagnostic note at the footer: `ℹ Sign in with "entire login" to see team comparisons.`
- **Labels still analyzing** — me side may be fully empty for labels/skills/tool mix (analyses in-flight). Team side may be full. Diagnostic note at the footer: `ℹ Labels require server analysis (may take a few minutes after committing).` Note renders only when at least one agent card has a team block but no me label data.

## Color & accessibility rules

- **Palette** — reuse existing `styles.go` constants. New additions: no colors added. `you` uses `colorAccent` (amber 214). `team` uses a new style `styles.team` bound to a magenta (say color `170`, matches the existing agents-panel magenta noted in earlier design docs).
- **`NO_COLOR=1`** — all amber/magenta/semantic styles become no-ops. The bars still render (they're Unicode geometry, not color-dependent). Prefixes still read correctly because they're plain text (`you`, `team`, `your`). Dot-pattern overlay `▒` is still visible against fill `█`. The view remains scannable without any color.
- **`ACCESSIBLE=1`** — drop box-drawing. Panels become `## Summary`, `## Activity`, `## Agents` sections with blank-line separators. Comparison bars degrade to `you: 2.9M / team: 1k` plain text lines — the bar glyph is skipped (screen readers would announce every cell). Everything else collapses to indented lists under the section headers.

## Concrete code changes

The spec maps to these file touches. An implementation plan will break these into ordered steps:

- `cmd/entire/cli/recap.go` — remove `--30` flag and `f.d30` field.
- `cmd/entire/cli/recap/model.go` — remove `Range30d` from the `RangeKey` enum (or keep the constant and map it to `RangeMonth` if any persisted state references it).
- `cmd/entire/cli/recap/render_static.go`
  - `renderHeader`: drop the `30d` tab option.
  - `renderSummaryBand`: rewrite to the new `you / team / top / context` shape.
  - `renderActivityStrip`: pad to full width, always render zero cells, annotate peak.
  - `renderBottomPanel`: delete (or inline a no-op). The entire bottom-panel code path is removed.
  - `RenderStatic`: drop the bottom-panel write.
- `cmd/entire/cli/recap/agents_card.go`
  - Rewrite the per-card renderer around the three-group structure.
  - Add a `renderComparisonBar` helper (me/team bar with overlay, proportional fill, readout).
  - Remove the `MCP servers` row, the `Distinct contribs` row.
  - Panel-level legend row emitted once per call, not per card.
- `cmd/entire/cli/recap/styles.go` — add `team lipgloss.Style` (magenta bold). Possibly add a helper `styles.prefixYou()` / `styles.prefixTeam()` to keep renderer call sites short.
- `cmd/entire/cli/recap/tui.go` — add `v` keybinding for view cycling. Update help text.

## Out of scope for v1

These are called out so reviewers don't ask "why isn't X in the spec":

- No drill-down overlay on an agent card. Enter-on-agent-row was part of the old design; keep postponed.
- No session list panel. Sessions surface in `entire sessions` today, no duplication needed.
- No per-day breakdown drill-down on the activity strip. Date ranges stay visual-only.
- Comparison bars are proportional within their own row, not normalized across all rows. Cross-row comparison isn't a stated goal.
- No unit tests for `renderComparisonBar` specifically in this spec — the plan will specify TDD for it.

1. **Comparison bars** — `tokens`, `sessions`, `checkpoints`.
   - Each row: label + bar + readout.
   - **Bar width formula**: `barWidth = innerPanelWidth - labelWidth - readoutWidth - 4` (4 = left indent + two padding gaps). `labelWidth = 12` (longest label "checkpoints" + padding). `readoutWidth = 14` (accommodates "2.9M / 999k").
   - **Minimum bar width**: 12 cells. Below that, the bar is dropped and the readout is rendered alone on the row (e.g. `tokens  2.9M / 1k`). This only matters below ~70 col terminals.
   - **Maximum bar width**: 40 cells, so even wide terminals don't stretch the bar past the visual sweet spot.
   - Bar fill: the larger side fills proportionally to `max(you, team)`. The smaller side overlays as dot pattern (`▒`) extending to its proportional length.
     - If `you > team`: amber fill `█` for `⌈you_ratio × width⌉` cells, magenta dots `▒` for `⌈team_ratio × width⌉` cells (overlaying the first N cells of the amber fill).
     - If `team > you`: flipped — magenta fill `█` for the team portion, amber fill `█` for the you portion at the start (shorter).
     - If `you == team` (both non-zero): amber fill full width; magenta dots overlay full width too. They alternate by priority (magenta wins on even columns, amber on odd) to make equality visible as a striped bar.
   - **Rounding**: any non-zero value gets a minimum of **1 cell** after rounding. Only `0` renders as empty cells in that region. This prevents tiny values (e.g. 1 session vs 1000) from visually disappearing.
   - Readout: `<you_value> / <team_value>`, human-formatted (`2.9M / 1k`, not `2901234 / 1045`). Use `formatTokens` for tokens; integers verbatim for sessions/checkpoints.
   - If a row has both sides zero, the **row drops entirely**. No `0 / 0` clutter.
   - If one side is nil (not zero — genuinely absent because the user isn't logged in or data hasn't synced), that side shows `—` in the readout but the bar renders as whatever data exists.

  - Accessible mode is **static-only output**. The TUI (bubbletea alt-screen + keybindings) is replaced by a one-shot render, so `v` and other keybindings are irrelevant in this path. Detection: `os.Getenv("ACCESSIBLE") != ""` forces `--format static` regardless of terminal capability.

### Minimum terminal width

- **Target**: 100–120 columns (common modern terminal).
- **Full fidelity down to 80 cols** — panels render normally; long skill/model lists soft-truncate more aggressively.
- **Between 70–80 cols** — comparison bars hit their 12-cell minimum, readouts stay intact. Panel borders still render.
- **Below 70 cols** — bars are dropped per the rule above. Panel output still works but is denser. No box-drawing fallback specifically for narrow terminals; the bottom-panel drop already compensates for vertical space.
- **Static output when piped** (`!isatty(stdout)`) — width defaults to 100 cols, matching the sweet spot.

input.new_string:
## Testing strategy

Every change below must land with the referenced tests green.

- **`renderComparisonBar` — new unit tests in `agents_card_test.go`**:
  - `you > team, both non-zero` — asserts amber-fill length + magenta-overlay length.
  - `team > you, both non-zero` — asserts the flipped fill.
  - `you == team, both non-zero` — asserts the striped pattern.
  - `you non-zero, team == 0` — asserts amber fill only, no overlay.
  - `you == 0, team non-zero` — asserts magenta fill only.
  - `you == 0, team == 0` — asserts nil return (caller drops the row).
  - `you tiny, team huge` (e.g. 1 vs 1000) — asserts `you` renders as 1-cell minimum (rounding floor).
  - `innerPanelWidth = 60` (narrow) — asserts bar width clamps to 12 min.
  - `innerPanelWidth = 200` (wide) — asserts bar width caps at 40 max.
- **Snapshot tests for static output** — one per view mode (`you`, `team`, `both`) at widths 80, 100, 140. Fixtures: one agent with full data, one with you-only, one with team-only, and the "no agent activity" empty-panel case. Use a frozen clock.
- **Summary panel shape tests** — assert the `top` line omits empty signals, drops entirely when all four are empty, and renders in the fixed order when multiple are present.
- **Activity strip tests** — assert zero-day cells render at the darkest shade, peak annotation renders in the correct format per range, peak is suppressed when all days are zero.
- **Accessible mode golden files** — one per panel, `NO_COLOR=1` + `ACCESSIBLE=1`. Assert no ANSI escapes, no box-drawing, no bar glyphs.
- **Sort determinism test** — build a view with two agents tied on `you_sessions + team_sessions`, assert alphabetical tie-break.
- **Drop behavior integration test** — build a view where one agent has team data but no me data, confirm the card drops the "your models/repos" block and the card still renders correctly.

Existing `agents_card_test.go`, `render_static_test.go`, and `contributors_test.go` will need updates for the new layout — prefer rewriting those assertions over adding new test files. TDD: write the failing test first, then the renderer change.

## Out of scope for v1
